58.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
58.solution: Percent atom economy = (formula weight of desired product / sum of formula weights of reactants) \(\times 100\). Here it is \(\frac{75}{225} \times 100 = 33.3\). So the answer is (B).

61.stemOverride: When tert-butyl bromide is heated with silver fluoride, the major product obtained is
61.solution: Heating an alkyl bromide with AgF is the Swarts reaction: F replaces Br on the same carbon. tert-Butyl bromide is \(\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\), so the product is \(\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{CF}\). Its name is 2-fluoro-2-methylpropane. So the answer is (B).

63.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
63.solution: Haemoglobin in blood forms a positively charged sol. Starch and gelatin sols are negative or neutral, and metal sols such as Ag are negatively charged. So the answer is (A).

68.stemOverride: Identify 'A' and 'B' in the following reaction. \(\text{CH}_3\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{AgNO}_2} A \xrightarrow{\text{Sn/HCl}} B\)
68.solution: \(\text{AgNO}_2\) is covalent, so it attacks through nitrogen and gives nitromethane, \(\text{CH}_3\text{NO}_2\) (A). Sn/HCl reduces the nitro group to an amino group, giving methylamine, \(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2\) (B). So the answer is (B).

71.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
71.stemOverride: Methyl propanoate on hydrolysis with dil NaOH forms a salt which on further acidification with conc. HCl forms
71.solution: Methyl propanoate, \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOCH}_3\), is saponified by NaOH to sodium propanoate and methanol. Acidifying with HCl converts sodium propanoate into propanoic acid, \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\). So the answer is (C).

72.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
72.solution: Benzene-1,2-diol is catechol, benzene-1,3-diol is resorcinol and benzene-1,4-diol is quinol. Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol. So the answer is (B).

73.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics

optionOverrides.D: For a chemical reaction to be spontaneous \(E^\circ_\text{cell}\) must be negative

73.solution: \(\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_\text{cell}\). A spontaneous reaction needs \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), so \(E^\circ_\text{cell}\) must be positive. The other statements are correct. So the answer is (D).

74.solution: Bohr's model allows only fixed orbits of fixed energy, with angular momentum a whole-number multiple of \(\frac{h}{2\pi}\). It cannot explain how atoms combine to form molecules by chemical bonds. So the answer is (D).

75.subtopic: Subatomic Particles, Isotopes, Isobars and Isoelectronic Species
75.solution: \(\text{Na}^+\) has \(11 - 1 = 10\) electrons. Ne also has 10 electrons, while F has 9, O has 8 and Mg has 12. So the answer is (D).

76.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
76.solution: Let rate \(= k[A]^x[B]^y\). Doubling [A] at constant [B] doubles the rate, so \(2^x = 2\) and \(x = 1\). So the answer is (C).

77.solution: Acid strength of the hydrogen halides rises as H-X bond strength falls: \(\text{HF} < \text{HCl} < \text{HBr} < \text{HI}\). The H-F bond is the strongest, so HF is the weakest acid. So the answer is (C).
